### A Gradual Transition

Think of waking as a gradual handoff, not a single switch. Later in the night, deep sleep gives way to lighter sleep and REM, which are easier to leave than deep N3. In self-awakening experiments, activity in the right prefrontal area shifted roughly 30 minutes beforehand, while heart rate rose about three minutes before waking. Different systems may join the transition at different times.

### Routine Can Shape the Pattern

This ability may also be strengthened by routine. In an 11-person home study, success reached 82% by the seventh day of trying to wake at the usual time without an alarm. A separate survey found that students who reported the habit kept sleep and wake times about 30 minutes earlier. The pattern may reflect expectation plus personal morningness, not an equally strong skill in everyone.

## In one line

A near-alarm awakening may be less like reading a clock than entering a familiar morning at the right moment.
